title: I started building Headlinne as a teenager because I was tired of the noise.
body:
It felt like every news app was designed to keep me angry or anxious. The algorithms were tuned to boost outrage rather than clarity. I knew there had to be a better way to stay informed without feeling overwhelmed by the endless scroll.

My goal was simple. I wanted to build a tool that respected my time and my intelligence. I started experimenting with AI not to replace journalism, but to filter out the clutter. The idea was to create a feed that actually learns what you care about, rather than just showing you what everyone else is clicking on.

Building this while still in school taught me a lot about focus. It is easy to get distracted by flashy features or engagement traps. It is much harder to build something that is genuinely useful every single day. We are still learning and iterating, but the core mission remains the same: give people control over their news feed.
cta: If you are ready for a cleaner way to read the news, you can try it out at HEADLINNE.com.
